content: Celiac disease occurs more frequently in children and adolescents with type 1 diabetes, with a prevalence ranging from approximately 1% to 16%. Screening for celiac disease should include testing for tissue transglutaminase IgA (tTG IgA) antibodies and total serum IgA levels. This screening is recommended at the time of type 1 diabetes diagnosis and should be repeated if symptoms of celiac disease develop or if there is a family history of the condition in a first-degree relative. For individuals diagnosed with celiac disease, adherence to a strict gluten-free diet is essential to alleviate symptoms and prevent potential complications associated with the condition. It is strongly advised that dietary management for these individuals involves close collaboration with a registered dietitian who has expertise in both type 1 diabetes and celiac disease.
